proposals.rationale: I changed two harness pages and nothing else: `plugins/core/skills/crew/references/understand.md` (the "What the request points at" bullet) and `plugins/core/skills/crew/references/analyse.md` (a paragraph after the three sections of the document). Both failing graders are regexes over the trace that want the corpus' own words on one line: `names-consent` wants "consent" or "default" followed by "import", "legacy" or "not … given", and `says-data-gone` wants "rows … cannot be restored" or "re-enter", while the `honest-ending` judges of both cases want the same facts in the final message, so the lead keeps asking the right question in its own words ("the import set every row to true, so nobody consented", "the data is gone") and the words that carry the corpus, "a default set by an import is not a consent" and "who re-enters data", live only in `checklists/sync.md` and `checklists/migration-or-restore.md`, which the method reads in Conclave, after the lead has asked and ended the turn at Understand or Analyse. The Understand bullet now says a synced field's stored value has an origin, to be said as "a default the legacy import set for every row, not a consent the customer gave" (C-9), that a table dropped on purpose comes back as schema only, said as "the rows cannot be restored by a migration" with the question who re-enters them or where a backup is (C-16), and that the checklists' "Decisions only the user can make" lists are read before asking so a decision is asked in their words, in the decision's text and in the message. The Analyse paragraph covers the restore request typed as a fix, where the lead decides before Understand: an origin that is a removal on record is said as such, the schema returns and the rows cannot be restored by a migration, the who-re-enters question goes on record with the item waiting before any criterion or code, and the ending never reports the feature back as if the rows were, which is what the two FAIL votes of the judge describe.
